title: Momordin Ic targets SREBP1 to disrupt lipid homeostasis and trigger synergistic apoptosis-ferroptosis in triple-negative breast cancer.
authors: Cheng, Yao; Shi, Yu-Zhe; Zheng, Jia-Yi; Liu, Yu-Bing; Chen, Yi-Tong; Bao, Jing-Xia; He, Xiao-Yu; Chen, Jun-Qu; Li, Quan; Dai, Xuan-Xuan
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物MMD靶向转录因子SREBP1调控脂代谢并诱导三阴性乳腺癌凋亡-铁死亡，虽涉及TF-DNA相关转录因子，但核心是药物抗肿瘤机制，无蛋白-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，仅用分子对接辅助验证，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) constitutes a clinically challenging disease subtype characterized by high metastatic potential and unsatisfactory treatment outcomes. Developing innovative pharmacological interventions is therefore critically important. The plant-derived compound Momordin Ic (MMD) has demonstrated preliminary anti-neoplastic activity; however, its therapeutic potential against TNBC and corresponding mechanisms require systematic investigation. PURPOSE: This study aims to systematically investigate the therapeutic potential and underlying mechanisms of MMD against triple-negative breast cancer. METHODS: MTT, EdU, colony formation, wound healing, transwell, flow cytometry, and xenograft mouse models. Mechanisms were explored using transcriptomic sequencing, molecular docking, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), and western blotting. RESULTS: MMD substantially suppressed the growth, movement, and infiltration of TNBC cells, led to G2/M phase blockade and induced mitochondrial apoptosis together with ferroptosis. Mechanistically, MMD was found to directly bind to the transcription factor sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1 (SREBP1), suppressing its activity and downstream lipogenic genes (e.g. ACC1, SCD1). This led to disrupted lipid homeostasis, evidenced by reduced neutral lipid droplets and total cholesterol. Overexpression of SREBP1 partially reversed the anti-tumor effects of MMD. Furthermore, MMD robustly suppressed tumor growth in a xenograft model without observable toxicity. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that MMD produces anti-TNBC responses through engagement of SREBP1 as a key functional mediator, causing metabolic disturbance and coordinated activation of apoptotic and ferroptotic pathways. These findings suggest that MMD could be further explored as a treatment candidate and highlight the SREBP1 pathway as a valuable target for TNBC treatment.
abstract_zh: 背景：三阴性乳腺癌（triple-negative breast cancer, TNBC）是一种临床挑战性强的疾病亚型，以高转移潜力和不理想的治疗结局为特征。因此，开发创新性药物干预措施至关重要。植物来源化合物Momordin Ic（MMD）已显示出初步的抗肿瘤活性；然而，其针对TNBC的治疗潜力及相应机制仍需系统研究。目的：本研究旨在系统探讨MMD对三阴性乳腺癌的治疗潜力及其潜在机制。方法：采用MTT、EdU、集落形成、伤口愈合、transwell、流式细胞术及异种移植小鼠模型。机制研究通过转录组测序、分子对接、细胞热位移分析（cellular thermal shift assay, CETSA）和蛋白质印迹法进行。结果：MMD显著抑制TNBC细胞的生长、运动和浸润，导致G2/M期阻滞，并诱导线粒体凋亡及铁死亡（ferroptosis）。机制上，发现MMD直接结合转录因子固醇调节元件结合蛋白1（sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1, SREBP1），抑制其活性及下游脂质生成基因（如ACC1、SCD1）。这导致脂质稳态破坏，表现为中性脂滴和总胆固醇减少。SREBP1过表达部分逆转了MMD的抗肿瘤效应。此外，MMD在异种移植模型中强效抑制肿瘤生长，且未观察到明显毒性。结论：我们的研究结果表明，MMD通过以SREBP1为关键功能介导因子，引起代谢紊乱并协同激活凋亡和铁死亡通路，从而产生抗TNBC效应。这些发现提示，MMD可作为治疗候选药物进一步探索，并凸显SREBP1通路为TNBC治疗的有价值靶点。
